analysis: integration/report.py: per solver, baseline vs linear and baseline vs boost separately; per-graph rows; solved categories; paired node/CPU/wall differences and ratios on jointly solved graphs only with graph bootstrap; timeouts as observed prefixes only
approval_token_rule: APPROVE- + first 16 hex digits of SHA-256 of this file
billing: standard GitHub-hosted runners are free for public repositories; Windows runners bill at 2x minutes only on private repositories
build: the exact build of a passing public validation run of the same commit (input validation_run), fetched from integration-results and hash-checked
expected_upper_runner_minutes_note: worst case assumes every invocation reaches its CPU limit and its wall equals the watchdog; Stage C observed wall ~= CPU + 1% for these single-threaded solvers
graph_set: all 130 graphs of tests/pace16-hidden at karek/FeedbackVertexSet-Experiments c0290698f6dfcc48b19b55e1aa915d8ecf61b0a4; IDs are listed (git ls-tree, no blobs) only inside the dispatched reserved workflow; each job checks out only its own graph file
job_layout: 3 static matrices (one per solver) of 130 jobs; each job = one graph, three policies sequentially on one runner

measurement.cooperative_stop: in-process at the CPU limit (checked at most every 10 ms of wall); driver kill at limit + 30 s -> cpu_timeout_forced
measurement.cpu: GetProcessTimes kernel+user of the whole solver process after exit
measurement.decisions: two-child branches (B); target decisions T; eligible decisions A (>=2 distinct eligible pivots; not measured in the timed baseline, which never enumerates candidates); scored decisions; departures (chosen != original pivot at the current state)
measurement.includes: process start, graph parsing, model loading (learned), search, feature extraction, scoring, output, summary write
measurement.nodes: entries to branching()/solve1()/solve2(), component subsolvers included (Stage C definition)
measurement.wall: driver perf_counter immediately before Popen to after wait()

models: integration/models/MODELS.json: the six frozen final refits of learnability run 45408454796 (results commit e5b8401), never retrained or reselected
retry_rule: A job is retried only after an infrastructure failure (wall_watchdog, not_run_job_deadline, driver_error, missing_record, build_mismatch, runner loss or a failed publish). The whole job (all three policies, same order) is re-run as a new attempt via "Re-run failed jobs"; at most 2 retries. Analysis uses, per job, the first attempt without an infrastructure failure, never mixing invocations of different attempts; after 3 failed attempts the job is reported as infrastructure_failure. Solver timeouts, solver errors, policy errors and verification failures are results and are never retried. Every attempt is preserved.
runner: windows-2025 (standard GitHub-hosted, 4 vCPU); one solver process at a time per runner
status: PROPOSED - graph set and compute budget require owner approval before dispatch

timing_repetitions.eligible: jobs in which all three policies complete with process CPU < 60 s
timing_repetitions.note: OPTIONAL and separately approved; NOT included in the 585 CPU-hour budget; same runner, rotated policy order (bench.py --timing-repetitions 2); primary records are never replaced; repetitions only estimate timing noise on short solves
